core_obligations: Reduce to the equalizer condition for a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes, using that the space is already a sheaf for the Zariski topology (proof lines 7064-7069).

Uniqueness: for two morphisms agreeing after composition with the covering, form the fibre product of the source with the space along the graph of the diagonal, observe that it is a monomorphism of schemes, that the covering factors through it, and that the projection from the base change of the monomorphism to the source is a monomorphism with a section and hence an isomorphism; conclude by descent of the property of being an isomorphism (proof lines 7071-7100).

Existence, choice of cover: find an etale morphism from a formal affine whose image contains the image of the given morphism, which uses compactness of the source and the fact that a finite union of formal affines is a formal affine, a small argument the author omits (proof lines 7102-7108).
Existence, base change: form the fibre product of that formal affine with the source over the space and note that it is an etale, separated and surjective morphism of schemes (proof lines 7108-7115).

Existence, descent datum: convert the cocycle condition on the given morphism into a descent datum on that morphism of schemes by an explicit chain of fibre product identifications (proof lines 7116-7133).

Existence, effectivity and descent: use that the morphism is etale and separated hence ind-quasi-affine, so that the descent datum is effective, obtain a morphism to the base that is surjective and etale by descent, build a morphism into the formal affine and descend it, and conclude the existence of a solution etale locally on the base (proof lines 7134-7160).
Existence, glueing: use uniqueness to see that the etale local solution satisfies the glueing condition and then the etale sheaf property to obtain a global solution (proof lines 7160-7165).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the equalizer condition (proof lines 7064-7069).
Uniqueness through the diagonal and descent of isomorphisms (proof lines 7071-7100).
Choice of an etale formal affine cover adapted to the given morphism (proof lines 7102-7108).
The etale separated surjective morphism obtained by base change (proof lines 7108-7115).
The descent datum and its effectivity (proof lines 7116-7138).
Descent of the morphism and its properties (proof lines 7138-7160).
Glueing via uniqueness and the etale sheaf property (proof lines 7160-7165).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that a formal algebraic space over a scheme is a sheaf for the fpqc topology (statement lines 7052-7059). The proof is organised as the equalizer condition for a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes, and it discharges the two halves of that condition by different mechanisms. Uniqueness is a fibre product argument: given two morphisms agreeing after composition with the covering, their difference is measured by the fibre product of the source with the graph of the diagonal, which is a monomorphism of schemes because the diagonal of a formal algebraic space is a representable monomorphism; the covering factors through it, whence the projection from the base change of this monomorphism to the source is a monomorphism with a section and therefore an isomorphism, and descent of the property of being an isomorphism makes the monomorphism itself an isomorphism, which is exactly the equality of the two morphisms (proof lines 7071-7100). Existence is a descent argument of a different kind and is the bulk of the proof: an etale cover of the target by a formal affine is chosen so as to contain the image of the given morphism, the base change of this cover along the given morphism is an etale separated surjective morphism of schemes, the cocycle condition for the given morphism is turned by an explicit chain of identifications into a descent datum on it, effectivity of that descent datum is obtained from the fact that the morphism is ind-quasi-affine because it is etale and separated, the descended morphism is checked to be surjective and etale by descent, a morphism into the chosen formal affine is produced and descended, and finally uniqueness from the first half upgrades the etale local solution to a global one because the space is an etale sheaf (proof lines 7102-7165). The claim is H3: at least four independent mechanisms are used -- fibred products with the diagonal, effectivity of an ind-quasi-affine descent datum, descent of surjectivity and etaleness, and the etale sheaf property -- and each has its own criterion.
